title: The Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS): A Framework for Ethical Integration of Generative AI in Educational Assessment
venue: Journal of University Teaching and Learning Practice
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how educational institutions should respond to the rapid spread of generative AI tools in assessment, especially the tension between banning these tools as academic misconduct and incorporating them in ways that support learning. The authors argue that a binary AI/no-AI stance is too simplistic and propose a practical framework for defining acceptable levels of GenAI use in assessments.

The main intervention is the Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS), a five-level scale ranging from no AI use to full AI use. The levels distinguish between idea generation/structuring, editing, task completion with human evaluation, and fully integrated use. The paper explains how the scale can help educators specify permitted AI use, support transparency, and guide students toward ethical and academically responsible use of GenAI in their work.

The paper is framed primarily around higher education assessment, but the authors state that the scale is flexible enough to be adapted for K-12 settings. It does not report an empirical study of student outcomes; instead, it synthesizes prior literature on GenAI, academic integrity, assessment design, and digital literacy. The paper concludes that institutions need clearer policies and more nuanced assessment designs that move beyond detection-and-punishment approaches toward structured, transparent integration of GenAI.

A relevant secondary contribution for K-12 and teacher-facing use is that the authors explicitly note GenAI's potential to support lesson planning, feedback, and assessment tasks, while also distinguishing educator use from student use in assessed work. However, the paper itself is not an evaluation of a classroom implementation or a teacher-training intervention.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative artificial intelligence / large language model tools capable of producing and revising text and other content, and supporting assessment-related tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper proposes the AI Assessment Scale (AIAS) for regulating how generative AI may be used in educational assessment, and discusses teacher/student uses such as brainstorming, editing, task completion, and feedback/support in assessment contexts.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/framework paper proposing the AI Assessment Scale rather than reporting an empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool. No study design, sample, or outcome data are presented.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has potential practical influence on assessment policy and GenAI integration, but it does not report measured impact on learning or operational outcomes. As a framework, its impact is suggestive rather than empirically demonstrated.
